newsitem.title: UK: Fannie Mae takes advantage of A$ demand.
newsitem.headline: Fannie Mae takes advantage of A$ demand.

text.p: The U.S. Federal National Mortgage Association (Fannie Mae) launched its second global bond denominated in Australian dollars on Thursday, boosting the amount following significant investor demand.
The 10-year bond was increased to A$1.0 billion from A$750 million due to the "phenomenal demand", Fannie Mae's director of long-term funding, Mehmood Nathani, told Reuters in a telephone interview.

"We have been keeping an eye on the (Australian dollar) market for some time," Nathani said. "The 10-year sector is where a lot of institutional investors have current holdings and are interested in buying."
Nathani said an interest rate cut in Australia on Wednesday had triggered the launch of the bond.

The Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA) cut official interest rates for the fifth time in a year, trimming its official cash rate by 50 basis points to 5.0 percent. "It gave the market a positive tone and there was strong interest in Australian government bonds, which made us feel even better about the demand that we thought would be there," Nathani said.
Demand for the issue was split approximately 55 percent into Europe, 25 percent into Asia and the balance into the U.S.
Nathani said there had been some switching out of government bonds and into this new 10-year global bond.
In June, Fannie Mae launched a A$1.0 billion five-year bond -- at the time the largest Australian dollar global bond -- to yield 19.5 basis points over government bonds.
This bond had last tightened to trade at around 12.5 b.p. over, dealers said.
Fannie Mae also launched the first New Zealand dollar bond for a U.S. agency in June.
